newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish racecourses to benefit from development fund.
newsitem.headline: Irish racecourses to benefit from development fund.

text.p: The Irish Horseracing Authority said on Wednesday it had created a capital development fund of 30 million Irish pounds aimed primarily at helping Ireland's racecourses improve their facilities.

"The fund is aimed primarily at assisting racecourses to improve their facilities, which in turn will will enable the industry to market horseracing more effectively," Denis Brosnan, Chairman of the IHA, said in a statement.

The IHA, which is responsible for the promotion and marketing of Irish racing, said it had endorsed an agreement establishing a loan facility of 15 million Irish pounds with Ulster Bank Markets to enable the fund to be created.
Brosnan said the key point in relation to the fund is that grants will be provided by the IHA on the basis of 50 percent of the cost of the approved projects.
"The Authority will have to be satisfied that racecourses have adequate resources to meet the balance of the cost or that necessary financing arrangements are in place," Brosnan said.
"An important objective of the fund is to assist racecourse to develop the full potential of their businesses," he added.

Brosnan said the IHA was examining development plans already submitted and added that decisions in relation to allocations from the fund would be made shortly. -- Damien Lynch, Dublin Newsroom +353 1 6603377
